f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: An alternative approach can be used if it satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss one, contact the FDA staff responsible for the guidance.
f.clause: Preamble (nonbinding statement)
f.applicability: Draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1): distributed for comment purposes only, not for implementation.

f.title: Make required SLCs even for non-marketed products unless approval is withdrawn or license revoked
f.statement: The SLC provisions of section 505(o)(4) apply to the listed drugs, including drugs that are not marketed, unless FDA has withdrawn approval of the NDA or ANDA with notice published in the Federal Register or, for a BLA, the biologics license has been revoked; an application holder not actively marketing the drug is still required to make applicable SLCs until then.
f.clause: I. Introduction
f.applicability: Draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1): distributed for comment purposes only, not for implementation. NDAs (505(b)), ANDAs (505(j)) where the RLD is not currently marketed, and BLAs (PHS Act 351); not OTC or marketed unapproved drugs.
f.exceptions: Not applicable once approval is withdrawn by Federal Register notice or the biologics license is revoked.

rows.actor: Application holder (NDA, BLA, or ANDA if the RLD is not currently marketed)
rows.quote: The SLC provisions in section 505(o)(4) apply to the above-listed drugs, including drugs that are 46 not marketed, unless FDA has withdrawn approval of the NDA or ANDA and notice of the 47 withdrawal has been published in the Federal Register, or, in the case of a BLA, the U.S. 48 biologics license to manufacture the biological product has been revoked. Thus, even if an 49 application holder is not actively marketing the drug(s) approved under its NDA, ANDA, or 50 BLA, it is required to make the applicable SLCs under section 505(o)(4) unless and until 51 approval of the application is effectively withdrawn in a Federal Register notice or the U.S. 52 biologics license to manufacture the product has been revoked.
rows.location: I. Introduction
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Scope/applicability duty to make SLCs for non-marketed products is proven by the quote; Draft guidance (nonbinding, not for implementation); quote carries margin line numbers.

f.title: FDA generally requires SLCs only for new information about a serious risk
f.statement: Reduced-effectiveness language added by the SUPPORT Act clarifies FDA can require labeling changes about a serious risk resulting from reduced effectiveness (including information from 505(o)(3) studies or trials); FDA generally intends to require labeling changes only when the new information is about a serious risk as defined in section 505-1.

f.applicability: Draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1): distributed for comment purposes only, not for implementation.

f.statement: Where Prescribing Information changes required under section 505(o)(4) necessitate changes to REMS documents and materials, the application holder should submit the REMS changes as REMS modifications.

f.title: Submit non-SLC safety-related labeling changes using standard supplement procedures
f.statement: Not all safety-related labeling changes (including reduced effectiveness) are required under 505(o)(4); e.g., new information about a nonserious risk does not meet SLC criteria. For changes not meeting SLC criteria, application holders may continue to submit labeling supplements using standard procedures (21 CFR 314.70 and 601.12).

f.applicability: Draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1): distributed for comment purposes only, not for implementation.

f.title: FDA to send SLC notification letters, on the same day to every holder when NSI affects several
f.statement: Once FDA determines that there is new safety information that should be included in labeling, it sends an SLC notification letter to the application holder(s); holders of approved NDAs, BLAs or ANDAs (if the RLD is not currently marketed) will be notified of the requirement to make the SLC unless approval has been formally withdrawn in a Federal Register notice or the biologics license is revoked. If the new safety information applies to more than one application holder, FDA intends to send a letter on the same day to each holder.
f.clause: III.A. How Will FDA Notify Application Holders of Required SLCs?
f.applicability: Draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1): distributed for comment purposes only, not for implementation.
f.exceptions: No notification once approval is withdrawn by Federal Register notice or the biologics license is revoked.

f.title: Comply with SLC notification letters for discontinued products unless approval is withdrawn
f.statement: Section 505(o)(4) requirements apply to NDAs, BLAs and ANDAs (if the RLD is not currently marketed), including discontinued products, unless approval has been withdrawn in the Federal Register or, for biologics, all aspects of the license are revoked; requirements in an SLC notification letter therefore apply unless approval has been withdrawn in the Federal Register.

f.title: Respond to an SLC notification letter with a labeling supplement or a rebuttal statement
f.statement: After receiving notification of the required SLC, the application holder must either submit a supplement with proposed labeling changes reflecting the new safety information, or notify FDA it does not believe a change is warranted and submit a statement detailing the reasons (a rebuttal statement).

f.statement: Within 15 days of the conclusion of the 30-day discussion period (and any extension), FDA will issue a supplement approval letter to any application holder with which it has reached agreement on the proposed labeling, and, where FDA and a holder cannot reach agreement on its proposed labeling changes or rebuttal, can order that holder to make the required labeling changes under section 505(o)(4)(E).

f.title: FDA discussion period on supplements or rebuttals lasts no more than 30 days unless extended
f.statement: If FDA disagrees with the language or placement in a submitted supplement or with a rebuttal's reasoning, FDA must initiate discussions that do not extend more than 30 days after receipt of the submission, unless FDA determines an extension is warranted.
